description: Somos amantes de la computación e informática, y lo que nos apasiona es crear tecnología útil para todos.
summary: Agro Planet is an application designed so that small farmers can decide what to plant and when to plant it using real information, not just intuition. Our application works as follows: the farmer enters the location of their land in the app, and the app begins gathering data on the climate, the soil, and the available water, relying on satellite information provided by NASA. With this data, it shows which crops are best suited and on which dates planting is recommended. If the crop the farmer wanted does not have good conditions; likewise, if the farmer wants to rent a plot of land, the app provides information about the characteristics of the land and the availability of resources so they can begin planting. Agro Planet proposes alternative crops, allowing the farmer to compare crops that are suited to the conditions of the chosen area, and it also sends alerts when unfavorable weather is expected. Its goal is for the farmer to be able to plan their season in advance, choose crops that truly suit their plot, and make more responsible use of the available resources, which helps reduce the risk of financial losses before investing in planting. Although tools such as CropSuit, GAEZ, PLANt, and the SENAMHI services already exist, what sets Agro Planet apart is that it does not just display data, but turns it into personalized recommendations for each plot of land, adapting to the empirical knowledge of small farmers.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

Agro Planet is an application that helps small farmers decide what to plant and when, using real data instead of intuition alone.

  • The farmer enters the location of their land in the app.
  • The app gathers data on climate, soil, and available water from NASA satellite information.
  • With that data, it recommends the most suitable crops and the planting dates.
  • If the crop the farmer wanted does not have good conditions, the app suggests alternatives and lets them compare them.
  • It sends alerts when unfavorable weather conditions are expected.
  • It can also be used to evaluate a plot of land before renting it, because it shows its characteristics and the available resources.

2. What benefits does it offer?

  • It helps plan agricultural seasons in advance.
  • It makes it easier to choose crops according to the characteristics of the land.
  • It promotes the responsible use of water.
  • It identifies agricultural alternatives when conditions are unfavorable, including crop rotation.
  • It reduces uncertainty before investing in a planting, and with it the risk of financial losses.

3. What is the expected impact of the project?

  • Economic: fewer losses for small farmers, because they make informed decisions before investing.
  • Environmental: better use of water and soil. The report gives two pieces of context: agriculture uses about 72% of the freshwater withdrawn worldwide, and around 33% of soils are degraded.
  • Social: it puts technical and satellite information within reach of farmers who lack technical knowledge or forecasting tools. About 1.2 billion people live in agricultural areas with severe water scarcity.
  • Validation: a pilot test on a plot in Ica is proposed. The app's recommendations will be compared with the judgment of a professional agronomist.
  • Monitoring indicators: climate risk percentage, water availability, land conditions, optimal planting period, crop compatibility under adverse conditions, and app usage rate.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software were used?

NASA data and tools:

  • GPM (Global Precipitation Measurement) and IMERG: precipitation
  • Landsat and MODIS: satellite imagery of soil and vegetation
  • NASA POWER: climate data
  • SRTM (Shuttle Radar Topography Mission): topography

Languages:

  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
  • Python

Python libraries: Pandas, Requests, Streamlit, Matplotlib, Plotly, and Folium.

Artificial intelligence:

  • ChatGPT, for document and information management.
  • Claude Code, for development using the spec-driven development methodology.

5. In what way is the project creative?

Similar tools already exist, such as CropSuit, GAEZ, and PLANt from the FAO, or SENAMHI's agroclimatic services. What sets Agro Planet apart is that it does not just display data: it turns them into personalized recommendations for each plot, adapted to the practical knowledge of small farmers. Its distinctive features are:

  • Personalized water diagnosis: compares the water available on the plot with the water each crop needs.
  • Alternative crop recommendation.
  • Dynamic agricultural calendar: combines climate history with updated forecasts.
  • Crop comparison tool: compares water needs, temperature, soil type, and cycle length.
  • Preventive alerts for adverse weather.
  • It brings together in a single app NASA satellite data that is normally scattered.

6. What factors did the team take into account?

  • Agro-environmental factors: climate (history and forecast), soil characteristics and degradation, water availability, and topography.
  • User needs: small farmers with little technical knowledge, so the information must be clear and visual.
  • Financial risk: avoiding losses before investing in a planting.
  • Existing solutions: CropSuit, GAEZ, PLANt, and SENAMHI were analyzed to avoid duplicating them and to contribute something new.
  • Feasibility: pilot test in Ica, with the owner's permission and a comparison of results with an agronomist.

Team profile:

  • Industrial engineering: processes and farmers' needs.
  • Software architecture: infrastructure.
  • Creative arts: interface and visual design.
  • Data analysis: data interpretation.
  • Systems engineering: development and integration of satellite data.
